claims.text: AM-fabricated MoNbTaW refractory HEAs exhibit intrinsic residual stresses.
AM-fabricated MoNbTaW refractory HEAs contain heterogeneous dislocation networks.
Deep cryogenic treatment at approximately -196 °C for 12–24 hours induces nano-twins in AM-fabricated MoNbTaW.
Deep cryogenic treatment homogenizes the dislocation network in AM-fabricated MoNbTaW.
The proposed nano-twins and homogenized dislocation network form within a BCC matrix.
Deep cryogenic treatment relieves internal residual stresses in AM-fabricated MoNbTaW.
Residual-stress relief and controlled nano-twinning spread plastic deformation more uniformly during loading.
Deep cryogenic treatment increases ductility by approximately 15–25% relative to untreated AM-fabricated MoNbTaW.
Deep cryogenic treatment produces a more uniform deformation response under dynamic loading.
The ductility and deformation-uniformity benefits extend to both quasi-static and dynamic impact conditions.
Compressive strength remains statistically comparable to that of untreated AM-fabricated MoNbTaW after deep cryogenic treatment.
Impact-induced energy release remains statistically comparable to that of untreated AM-fabricated MoNbTaW after deep cryogenic treatment.
Untreated AM-fabricated MoNbTaW has lower uniform ductility and more localized deformation because of residual-stress concentrations.
The enhancement occurs only within an optimized treatment window around -196 °C for 12–24 hours.
Departures from the proposed treatment window may fail to produce the desired microstructural changes.
Departures from the proposed treatment window may trigger detrimental phase transformations that compromise energetic characteristics.
Microstructural theories and analogous studies suggest that deep cryogenic treatment can improve ductility.
